lines.raw: Think about your phone's **contact list**.

lines.say: Each contact has a name, a number, maybe an address and a note like "plumber" or "dentist".

lines.raw: Insurance data works the same way.

lines.say: A claim only carries a provider's I D number, for example 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 3.

lines.raw: To know that this number means "Lakeside General Hospital, a general acute care hospital in Texas, in Emily's network", the insurer looks it up in its **provider data**.
lines.say: To know that this number means "Lakeside General Hospital, a general acute care hospital in Texas, in Emily's network", the insurer looks it up in its provider data.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Simple definition.
lines.say: Simple definition.

lines.raw: Provider data is the record of **every doctor, hospital, clinic, lab and pharmacy** the insurer deals with: **who they are**, **what kind of care they give**, **where they are**, **which IDs they use**, and **whether they have a contract** with the insurer.
lines.say: Provider data is the record of every doctor, hospital, clinic, lab and pharmacy the insurer deals with: who they are, what kind of care they give, where they are, which I D's they use, and whether they have a contract with the insurer.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Where this fits.
lines.say: Where this fits.

lines.raw: A provider can be a **person** or an **organization**, and claims name providers in roles: **rendering** (did the work), **billing** (gets paid), **referring**, **ordering** and **attending**.
lines.say: A provider can be a person or an organization, and claims name providers in roles: rendering (did the work), billing (gets paid), referring, ordering and attending.

lines.raw: The **Medical** course explains these roles on the claim.
lines.say: The Medical course explains these roles on the claim.

lines.raw: This course goes one level deeper: the provider list itself.
lines.say: This course goes one level deeper: the provider list itself.

lines.raw: Meet our people.
lines.say: Meet our people.

lines.raw: This course follows three people.
lines.say: This course follows three people.

lines.raw: **Ram** works at a tech startup in Kathmandu and has private group health insurance: he pays the hospital first, then claims the money back.
lines.say: Ram works at a tech startup in Kathmandu and has private group health insurance: he pays the hospital first, then claims the money back.

lines.raw: **Sita** is an accountant in Kathmandu who contributes to the Social Security Fund (SSF) and uses SSF-listed hospitals.
lines.say: Sita is an accountant in Kathmandu who contributes to the Social Security Fund (S S F) and uses S S F listed hospitals.

lines.raw: **Emily** is an office worker in Austin, Texas (member ID M1001) on her employer's PPO plan.
lines.say: Emily is an office worker in Austin, Texas (member I D M 1 0 0 1) on her employer's P P O plan.

lines.raw: In 2025 she saw her family doctor, **Dr. Patel**, for strep throat, and had her appendix removed at **Lakeside General Hospital**.
lines.say: In 2025 she saw her family doctor, Doctor Patel, for strep throat, and had her appendix removed at Lakeside General Hospital.

lines.raw: Later in the course we also meet Emily's father, **Robert**.
lines.say: Later in the course we also meet Emily's father, Robert.

lines.raw: Provider data in Nepal.
lines.say: Provider data in Nepal.

lines.raw: In Nepal: How Ram and Sita know who treated them.
lines.say: In Nepal: How Ram and Sita know who treated them.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: Every doctor in Nepal must be registered with the **Nepal Medical Council (NMC)** and gets an **NMC registration number**.
lines.say: Every doctor in Nepal must be registered with the Nepal Medical Council (N M C) and gets an N M C registration number.

lines.raw: You often see it on the doctor's nameboard, prescription pad or stamp.
lines.say: You often see it on the doctor's nameboard, prescription pad or stamp.

lines.raw: Nurses, pharmacists and other health workers register with their own councils, such as the **Nepal Nursing Council** and the **Nepal Pharmacy Council**.
lines.say: Nurses, pharmacists and other health workers register with their own councils, such as the Nepal Nursing Council and the Nepal Pharmacy Council.

lines.raw: Ram's private insurer may keep a list of hospitals where it has an arrangement, and checks the hospital name, **PAN** and the doctor's NMC number on the receipts he sends.
lines.say: Ram's private insurer may keep a list of hospitals where it has an arrangement, and checks the hospital name, P A N and the doctor's N M C number on the receipts he sends.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: SSF publishes a list of **listed (empanelled) hospitals** where members like Sita can be treated.
lines.say: S S F publishes a list of listed (empanelled) hospitals where members like Sita can be treated.

lines.raw: That list is SSF's **provider data**: hospital name, location and what services it offers.
lines.say: That list is SSF's provider data: hospital name, location and what services it offers.

lines.raw: When the hospital sends Sita's claim, SSF can match it to an entry on its list.
lines.say: When the hospital sends Sita's claim, S S F can match it to an entry on its list.

lines.raw: A hospital that is not on the list is not paid directly.
lines.say: A hospital that is not on the list is not paid directly.

lines.raw: In the US: Provider data for Emily's insurer in Texas.
lines.say: In the U S: Provider data for Emily's insurer in Texas.

lines.raw: Emily's insurer keeps a **provider master file**: one central list of every provider it knows about.
lines.say: Emily's insurer keeps a provider master file: one central list of every provider it knows about.

lines.raw: Each entry holds the provider's **NPI** (national ID), **name**, **type**, **specialty**, **addresses**, **tax ID**, **licence** and **network status**.
lines.say: Each entry holds the provider's N P I (national I D), name, type, specialty, addresses, tax I D, licence and network status.

lines.raw: When claim **23098908** arrives with Dr. Patel's NPI, the insurer looks her up: is she real, is she a family doctor, is she **in-network** for Emily's plan?
lines.say: When claim 23098908 arrives with Doctor Patel's N P I, the insurer looks her up: is she real, is she a family doctor, is she in-network for Emily's plan?

lines.raw: Members see a friendly version of this list as the **provider directory**: the "Find a Doctor" search on the insurer's website.
lines.say: Members see a friendly version of this list as the provider directory: the "Find a Doctor" search on the insurer's website.

lines.raw: Master data vs. event data.
lines.say: Master data versus event data.

lines.raw: Analysts split healthcare data into two kinds.
lines.say: Analysts split healthcare data into two kinds.

lines.raw: **Events** happen again and again: a visit, a prescription, a payment.
lines.say: Events happen again and again: a visit, a prescription, a payment.

lines.raw: **Master data** (also called **reference data** or a **dimension**) describes the people and things involved, and changes slowly.
lines.say: Master data (also called reference data or a dimension) describes the people and things involved, and changes slowly.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Examples. Event data: Medical claims, pharmacy claims, payments. Master data: Member list (eligibility), **provider list**, code lists.
lines.say: Examples. Event data: Medical claims, pharmacy claims, payments. Master data: Member list (eligibility), provider list, code lists.

lines.raw: How it grows. Event data: New rows every day. Master data: Changes slowly: a new doctor joins, an address changes.
lines.say: How it grows. Event data: New rows every day. Master data: Changes slowly: a new doctor joins, an address changes.

lines.raw: Question it answers. Event data: "What happened?". Master data: "Who or what is this?".
lines.say: Question it answers. Event data: "What happened?". Master data: "Who or what is this?".

lines.raw: Emily example. Event data: Claim 23098908 on 10 Mar 2025. Master data: Dr. Patel: family medicine, Sunrise Family Clinic, in-network.
lines.say: Emily example. Event data: Claim 23098908 on 10 Mar 2025. Master data: Doctor Patel: family medicine, Sunrise Family Clinic, in-network.

lines.raw: Nepal example. Event data: Ram's hospital bill. Master data: The NMC register of doctors.
lines.say: Nepal example. Event data: Ram's hospital bill. Master data: The N M C register of doctors.

lines.raw: Why analysts care.
lines.say: Why analysts care.

lines.raw: Claims tell you **how much** was spent.
lines.say: Claims tell you how much was spent.

lines.raw: Provider data tells you **with whom**.
lines.say: Provider data tells you with whom.

lines.raw: Without it you cannot answer questions like "Which hospitals cost the most?", "How much do we spend on cardiologists?" or "Are members using in-network doctors?".
lines.say: Without it you cannot answer questions like "Which hospitals cost the most?", "How much do we spend on cardiologists?" or "Are members using in-network doctors?".

lines.say: An insurer builds its provider master file by combining several:

scenes.section: Where US provider data comes from

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **NPPES** (the national NPI registry, run for CMS). What it gives: NPI, name, provider type, taxonomy (specialty), practice address. Public and free to search. Nepal comparison: The NMC register of doctors.
lines.say: N P P E S (the national N P I registry, run for C M S). What it gives: N P I, name, provider type, taxonomy (specialty), practice address. Public and free to search. Nepal comparison: The N M C register of doctors.

lines.raw: **Credentialing** records. What it gives: Checked licences, education, board certification, history of problems. Nepal comparison: Checking a doctor's NMC certificate and degrees before hiring.
lines.say: Credentialing records. What it gives: Checked licences, education, board certification, history of problems. Nepal comparison: Checking a doctor's N M C certificate and degrees before hiring.

lines.raw: **Contracts** with the insurer. What it gives: Network status, start and end dates, agreed prices. Nepal comparison: SSF's agreement with a listed hospital.
lines.say: Contracts with the insurer. What it gives: Network status, start and end dates, agreed prices. Nepal comparison: SSF's agreement with a listed hospital.

lines.raw: **Claims** themselves. What it gives: Which NPIs actually bill, and from which addresses. Nepal comparison: Receipts Ram sends in.
lines.say: Claims themselves. What it gives: Which N P I's actually bill, and from which addresses. Nepal comparison: Receipts Ram sends in.

lines.raw: **Provider updates**. What it gives: New phone, new address, accepting new patients or not. Nepal comparison: A clinic putting up a "we have moved" sign.
lines.say: Provider updates. What it gives: New phone, new address, accepting new patients or not. Nepal comparison: A clinic putting up a "we have moved" sign.

lines.raw: Step 1: Doctor gets an NPI.
lines.say: Step 1: Doctor gets an N P I.

lines.raw: Dr. Patel applies through NPPES once in her career and receives her 10-digit NPI.
lines.say: Doctor Patel applies through N P P E S once in her career and receives her 10-digit N P I.

lines.raw: Step 2: Insurer checks her.
lines.say: Step 2: Insurer checks her.

lines.raw: Emily's insurer **credentials** her: licence, training, history.
lines.say: Emily's insurer credentials her: licence, training, history.

lines.raw: Step 3: Contract signed.
lines.say: Step 3: Contract signed.

lines.raw: Sunrise Family Clinic signs a contract, so Dr. Patel becomes **in-network**.
lines.say: Sunrise Family Clinic signs a contract, so Doctor Patel becomes in-network.

lines.raw: Step 4: Added to the master file.
lines.say: Step 4: Added to the master file.

lines.raw: The insurer creates her provider record and shows her in the directory.
lines.say: The insurer creates her provider record and shows her in the directory.

lines.raw: Step 5: Claims match.
lines.say: Step 5: Claims match.

lines.raw: Every claim with her NPI is linked to that record and paid at the contracted price.
lines.say: Every claim with her N P I is linked to that record and paid at the contracted price.

scenes.section: Where US provider data comes from

lines.raw: Provider data goes out of date quickly.
lines.say: Provider data goes out of date quickly.

lines.raw: Doctors move clinics, retire, stop taking new patients or leave a network.
lines.say: Doctors move clinics, retire, stop taking new patients or leave a network.

lines.raw: A directory that lists doctors who cannot actually be booked is sometimes called a **"ghost network"**.
lines.say: A directory that lists doctors who cannot actually be booked is sometimes called a "ghost network".

lines.raw: US rules now require plans to verify directory details regularly, so keeping provider data fresh is a real, ongoing job.
lines.say: U S rules now require plans to verify directory details regularly, so keeping provider data fresh is a real, ongoing job.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Provider data is the list of who gives care: name, type, specialty, address, IDs and network status.
lines.say: Provider data is the list of who gives care: name, type, specialty, address, I D's and network status.

lines.raw: Claims are events; the provider list is master (reference) data that explains the IDs on each claim.
lines.say: Claims are events; the provider list is master (reference) data that explains the I D's on each claim.
